# cyclingpower

Compare the readings of two or three power meters that recorded the same
riding. Reads FIT, GPX and CSV files, puts them on a common clock, and
reports how far apart the meters are overall and across the power range.
A third meter that never rode alongside the others can be linked in
through a bridge meter common to both sessions.

## Installation

``` r

remotes::install_github("jzuccollo/cyclingpower")
```

FIT files need [FITfileR](https://github.com/grimbough/FITfileR), which
is not on CRAN. It is declared in `Remotes:` so the command above
fetches it. GPX and CSV need nothing extra. The app needs a few more
packages:

``` r

install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "DT", "shinyFiles"))
```

## Usage

Name your files `<run>_<source>`, so `run1_kickr.fit` is the Kickr’s
recording of run one, and hand
[`read_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/read_rides.md)
the directory they are in.

``` r

library(cyclingpower)

aligned <- read_rides("rides") |> align_rides()

power_agreement(aligned)      # overall difference, in watts and per cent
agreement_by_level(aligned)   # the same, across the power range
chain_sources(aligned)        # meters linked through a common bridge meter
```

[`power_agreement()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/power_agreement.md)
leads with the answer and keeps the arithmetic underneath:

    run1: assioma reads 2.6% higher than kickr (95% CI 2.4 to 2.7, from 1,800 seconds)

Where the filenames do not carry the labels, build the table yourself
with
[`ride_spec_from_names()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/ride_spec_from_names.md)
or by hand and pass that instead.
[`compare_report()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/compare_report.md)
runs the whole pipeline and writes an HTML report:

``` r

compare_report("rides", "power-comparison.html")
```

To see all of it working on rides with known errors planted in them, run
[`demo_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/demo_rides.md)
and follow
[`vignette("cyclingpower")`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/articles/cyclingpower.md).

## The app

[`launch_app()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/launch_app.md)
opens a local web interface over the same pipeline: pick a directory,
fix the run and source labels if the filenames don’t carry them, and
adjust settings live. **Load demo rides** builds a worked example with
known errors planted, also available outside the app from
[`demo_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/demo_rides.md).

The app can also record the meters itself over Web Bluetooth (Chrome or
Edge, Record tab). One clock stamps every sample, so the sources share a
timebase by construction. The radio path has no automated tests, so
check the first session against a head unit you trust.

## Recording

If each meter records to its own head unit, then on every unit: record
every second (not “smart” recording), turn auto-pause off, let the clock
set from GPS, and zero the meter after a warm-up. Ride four to six short
surges from coasting so
[`align_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/align_rides.md)
has features to cross-correlate, then five or six steady steps across
the power range so
[`agreement_by_level()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/agreement_by_level.md)
has seconds in each bin.

Recording in the app changes this: an erg ladder up and back down
through five targets is now the best ride rather than the worst, since
the offset is zero by construction. Keep a short block of surges anyway
— `check_alignment()` cannot distinguish a featureless ride from a
correctly stamped one, so the surges are what make a resolved zero mean
something.

[`vignette("recording_rides")`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/articles/recording_rides.md)
has the full protocol for both routes.

## Why alignment comes first

Independent head units can differ by several seconds. Differencing on
nominal timestamps then compares one moment’s power against another’s,
which inflates the spread and shifts the mean difference — and the
result looks plausible. On a test ride with a true 3 per cent gain and a
seven-second offset, differencing raw timestamps reports 6.2 per cent.

[`align_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/align_rides.md)
recovers the offset by cross-correlating the power traces and reports
what it found. Where a ride was too steady to lock onto it says so and
falls back to the recorded timestamps rather than guessing.

## Chaining a third meter

Run one carries meters A and B, run two carries B and C, and you want A
against C. B is the bridge: each run gives a gain relative to it, and
the difference between those gains is A against C.
[`chain_sources()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/chain_sources.md)
marks these as `chained` rather than `direct`, because they assume B
read the same on both days — which the ride files cannot test.
[`chain_report()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/chain_sources.md)
states the assumption and reports whether the two runs covered
comparable power.

## Stability

Version 0.4.0, and the version number is doing real work: the analysis
functions —
[`read_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/read_rides.md),
[`align_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/align_rides.md),
[`power_agreement()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/power_agreement.md),
[`agreement_by_level()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/agreement_by_level.md),
[`chain_sources()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/chain_sources.md)
and the plots — are settled and changes to them will be listed in
[NEWS.md](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/NEWS.md). The
recording half is newer and its shape may still move. The radio path has
no automated tests and cannot have any, so check your first recorded
session against a head unit you trust before relying on it.

which explains how the package is tested and what in the recorder must
not be simplified.

# Package index

## Reading rides

Get files onto one schema. Every reader returns the same shape whatever
the container format.

- [`read_file()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/read_file.md)
  : Read a ride file
- [`read_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/read_rides.md)
  : Read several ride files into one long tibble
- [`ride_spec_from_names()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/ride_spec_from_names.md)
  : Build a ride spec from filenames
- [`demo_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/demo_rides.md)
  : Write a set of demonstration ride files

## Aligning

Put the sources on a common one-second clock. Everything downstream
assumes this has happened.

- [`align_rides()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/align_rides.md)
  [`alignment_report()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/align_rides.md)
  : Put sources onto a common one-second clock

## Comparing

How far apart two meters read, overall and across the power range. All
intervals come from a moving-block bootstrap.

- [`power_agreement()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/power_agreement.md)
  : How far apart two meters read
- [`agreement_by_level()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/agreement_by_level.md)
  : How the difference between two meters varies with power
- [`level_dependence()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/level_dependence.md)
  : Whether a pair's error changes across the power range
- [`print(`*`<cyclingpower_agreement>`*`)`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/cyclingpower_print.md)
  [`print(`*`<cyclingpower_chain>`*`)`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/cyclingpower_print.md)
  : The answer, before the table

## Chaining

Meters that never rode together, linked through one that rode with both.

- [`chain_sources()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/chain_sources.md)
  [`chain_report()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/chain_sources.md)
  : Put meters from different rides on one scale
- [`chain_by_level()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/chain_by_level.md)
  : How the chained comparison varies with power
- [`bridge_candidates()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/bridge_candidates.md)
  : Sources that could bridge two runs

## Charts and reports

- [`plot_timeseries()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/plot_timeseries.md)
  : Power over time, by source
- [`plot_agreement()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/plot_agreement.md)
  : Bland-Altman plot of the difference between two meters
- [`plot_by_level()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/plot_by_level.md)
  : Difference between two meters across the power range
- [`plot_chain()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/plot_chain.md)
  : Gains between meters on one scale
- [`compare_report()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/compare_report.md)
  : Render the whole comparison from a set of files
- [`launch_app()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/launch_app.md)
  : Explore a comparison interactively

## Recording a comparison

The session to ride, as data rather than prose, and as a file a trainer
app can follow.

- [`comparison_protocol()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/comparison_protocol.md)
  : The session to ride for a comparison
- [`collapse_protocol()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/collapse_protocol.md)
  : The protocol as blocks to read
- [`write_workout()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/write_workout.md)
  : Write the protocol as a trainer workout file

## Ride metrics

The Coggan definitions, and a simulator that hits a chosen NP and AP.

- [`average_power()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/average_power.md)
  : Average power
- [`intensity_factor()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/intensity_factor.md)
  : Intensity factor
- [`normalised_power()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/normalised_power.md)
  : Normalised power
- [`tss()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/tss.md) :
  Training stress score
- [`variability_index()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/variability_index.md)
  : Variability index
- [`simulate_power()`](https://jzuccollo.github.io/cyclingpower/reference/simulate_power.md)
  : Simulate a power series with a given average and normalised power
